version.value: Original string-orchestra work, all three movements
version.note: The original label identifies Symphony No. 5 in B minor and lists all three movements. The score has two violin parts, viola and figured bass. The edition, continuo realisation and orchestral parts used in this session are unknown. The modern critical edition supplies the musical observations; it postdates the recording.

performers.note: The side-two label gives these performers specifically for the symphony. Martin Galling, Klaus Pohlers, Georg Schmid and Reinhold Buhl are credited separately for the quartet on the same side; the item-wide list of artists is therefore insufficient to identify the symphony’s individual players.

date.note: No session date is established. The January 1961 review provides a documented upper bound; the Archive dates the issue 1959 and the sleeve bears a 1959 copyright notice. The 2022 scan and transfer dates concern the archival copy.

place.note: The original side-two label states ‘Rec. in Germany’. City, venue and studio are unknown.

label.note: Monaural US vinyl LP, The Sons of Bach, Vol. I: Symphonies and Chamber Music. The sleeve bears a 1959 Vox Productions copyright notice.

catalogue.note: Catalogue number printed on the sleeve and both labels, matching the Internet Archive carrier metadata.

matrixTakeSides.value: Side 2, band 1; printed side identifiers DL 463-1 B and M-1118-B
matrixTakeSides.note: These identifiers are transcribed from the label. Runout inscriptions, stamper, session take and original tape number are unknown. The label gives the symphony’s duration as 12:33; the selected digital transfer lasts 758.93 seconds.

credits.value: Internet Archive LP transfer; operator account associate-klentjohn-postanes
credits.note: The operator is identified only by the archive account. The sleeve’s separate credit ‘Mastering: Dr. R. van Gelder’ concerns the historical LP.

date.note: Transcribed from ripping_date 20221029092156. The artwork scan is dated 26 October 2022. Neither date identifies the performance session.

processing.value: Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; 24-bit FLAC side transfer and segmented VBR MP3 derivative.
processing.note: Equipment comes from the item’s lineage field; the file list identifies the FLAC side and MP3 track. Equalisation, de-clicking, pitch correction and noise reduction settings are unknown.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a monaural vinyl LP transfer

composition.value: Underlying composition is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms.
composition.note: Bach composed the symphony in 1773 and died in 1788. Copyright in the modern critical edition is separate; its score is cited for research and is not reproduced here.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis: lawful commercial publication no later than January 1961, before 1963.
recording.note: HiFi/Stereo Review reviewed this exact Vox catalogue and performance in January 1961. Internet Archive dates the issue 1959, corroborated by the sleeve’s 1959 copyright notice, but the rights assessment uses the independently documented 1961 publication bound. Under the project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule, the former 50-year phonogram term expired before the extension applied on 1 November 2013. US recording rights remain unestablished. Internet Archive supplies no Creative Commons licence. Clearance here is territorial, not worldwide.

rights.creditLine: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach, Symphony in B minor, Wq 182/5; Mainzer Kammerorchester, Günter Kehr. Vox DL 463-1 (mono, dated 1959; commercially available by January 1961), side 2, band 1; Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US recording status not established.

sources.title: Vox DL 463-1 — original sleeve and labels
sources.locator: PDF page 2: copyright 1959, monaural carrier and mastering credit. Page 4: side-two label, band 1, all three symphony movements, Mainzer Kammerorchester, Günter Kehr, ‘Rec. in Germany’, DL 463-1 B and M-1118-B. Label and sleeve inspected visually. Robert Cushman’s sleeve notes incorrectly describe the Wq 182 symphonies as published in 1773; the modern critical introduction establishes their manuscript circulation.

sources.title: C. P. E. Bach: The Complete Works, III/2 — Symphony V in B minor
sources.locator: Edited by Sarah Adams, 2006, printed pp. 60–73. Openings of all three movements, Larghetto dynamics on pp. 67–68, and Presto repeat signs and ending on pp. 70 and 73 inspected visually. Musical cues describe whole movements or their opening paragraphs; no bar-by-bar timing or ear review is asserted.

sources.locator: Lists the three Kehr movements as 4:30, 3:44 and 4:20.
